newsitem.title: UK: British-Borneo set for big drilling project.
newsitem.headline: British-Borneo set for big drilling project.

text.p: British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc, the UK exploration and production group, said on Thursday it is embarking on its most ambitious drilling programme ever.
The UK independent expects to participate in around 30 exploration and appraisal wells this year.
"It's certainly our biggest programme in terms of the net reserves which we're going to be exposed to," finance director Bill Colvin said in a telephone interview.
British-Borneo will be involved in between 10 and 15 wells in the deepwater Gulf of Mexico and between 10 and 12 in the UK North Sea, he said.
"It's a very active year for us," Colvin said.
The group plans to spend up to 75 million pounds ($120.2 million) on its expanded exploration and appraisal programme this year and a further 100 million pounds on development projects.
"We remain confident that there are many further opportunities to be pursued in our chosen area of focus," the company said in a statement accompanying the results.

British-Borneo announced a jump in pretax profits to 19.51 million pounds in the year to December 31, 1996, up from 13.63 million the year before. Net profit rose by 38 percent to 14.4 million pounds. Its dividend for the year rose by 10 percent to 8.25 pence per share.
"The results were reasonably good, obviously helped by pretty good U.S. oil and gas prices," said Colvin.
"The underlying business was nice and solid last year and continues looking good as we go forward."
Colvin said that the highlight of last year's group performance was the successful completion and testing of the Morpeth field in the Gulf of Mexico.
"That was a massive achievement...it was one of the best wells ever completed and tested in the deepwater Gulf of Mexico and we did it as the operator".
Development of Morpeth is now underway, and a further three discoveries are under appraisal.
In the North Sea. the successful appraisal of the Mariner heavy oilfield continues.
British-Borneo has been one of the best-performing shares on the London stock exchange this year, reflecting talk that exploration minnow was ripe for a takeover bid.

But Colvin said the company had not been approached and he had no worries on that score. "We're absolutely delighted with the way the market has taken our story and performance and we don't have any fears (of a takeover bid)...We're just trying to focus 100 percent on growing the business and doing additional deals in the Gulf and growing our exploration and appraisal portfolio," he said.
British-Borneo shares were up 2-1/2 pence at 1,461 pence at 0940 GMT, down from an earlier high of 1,480.
